ai.title: Trim CLI welcome screen and limit agent preview to 3
ai.summary: Removed client environment variable dump from CLI welcome screen in `cli/src/chat.tsx`, relying on explicit `marginTop`/`marginBottom` spacing after ASCII logo instead of manual newlines. `TRUNCATE_LIMIT` for agent previews reduced from 5 to 3 in `cli/src/components/message-block.tsx`. Scope covers CLI chat rendering and message block components. Environment variable display logic now depends solely on SDK client availability.

eli5.text: When you start the command-line tool, the opening screen no longer displays a list of your environment variables; instead of stacking manual blank lines before the ASCII logo, it now uses built-in spacing, so the logo still has a small gap above it but the technical configuration details are gone. You will see the logo followed directly by the chat interface, without a block of settings information first. Additionally, when the tool previews code suggestions, it shows at most three examples instead of five, making each preview shorter. These changes are live today.

ai.title: Remove SDK environment section from CLI welcome message
ai.summary: Deleted SDK environment variable display logic from `cli/src/chat.tsx`. Removed `getCodebuffClient` import and associated block generation for raw/computed env vars. Streamlines welcome message output by eliminating verbose diagnostic info.

eli5.text: The welcome message you see when opening the command-line assistant no longer dumps a long list of technical environment variables at the top of your screen. That diagnostic block, showing raw settings and computed values, has been removed, so the greeting comes on cleaner and skips the clutter. You’d notice a shorter, less busy startup screen. Live today.

ai.title: QuadraticScrollAccel replaces createChatScrollAcceleration in CLI chat
ai.summary: New `QuadraticScrollAccel` class implements `ScrollAcceleration` using a rolling time window and `Queue` utility to calculate tick averages, replacing the factory function in `cli/src/chat.tsx`. A shared `clamp` helper was extracted into new `cli/src/utils/math.ts`, while `cli/src/utils/arrays.ts` gained `repeated` and a ring-buffer `Queue` implementation. The change affects only CLI chat scrolling behavior; no Web/Desktop surfaces modified.

eli5.text: When you're chatting in the terminal and messages scroll past, the speed now changes smoothly based on how fast you're scrolling, instead of jumping at a steady rate. You'll notice that flicking through a long conversation feels more natural and less jerky, while casual scrolling stays controlled. The change only affects the terminal chat window, so your browser or desktop app behave exactly as before.

ai.title: best-of-n planner prompts gain code style nits
ai.summary: Code style notes added to plan-selector and best-of-n-implementor prompts. Covers sparse try/catch, required args over optional, new components in new files. Internal agent guidance only.

eli5.text: The internal system that writes code for you now gets a bit more guidance on how to write that code cleanly. When it's planning and then building your requested feature, it's been told to avoid unnecessary error-handling blocks, prefer clear required inputs over optional ones, and put new pieces of code into their own files rather than tacking them onto existing ones. Nothing changes for you today unless you're directly editing these planning instructions, but the code your assistant eventually writes might look a little tidier because of it.

ai.title: CLI message block ancestor prefix simplification
ai.summary: The CLI message block renderer now skips the first level of ancestor branches when constructing prefixes. This change reduces visual clutter by replacing vertical bars with spaces for all ancestors except the deepest one. The modification is isolated to `cli/src/components/message-block.tsx`.

eli5.text: The assistant's reply previews in the terminal now show fewer vertical lines, making the conversation tree easier to read. Only the deepest branch level is drawn as lines and corners, while all earlier ancestor levels are blank spaces instead. You would notice cleaner, less cluttered indentation whenever the assistant builds a multi-step plan.

ai.title: CLI: remove scrollToAgent and agentRefsMap
ai.summary: Deleted `scrollToAgent` logic and `agentRefsMap` tracking from the CLI chat interface. This removes the automatic scroll-to-anchor behavior when toggling agent or tool branches, simplifying `useChatScrollbox` and `MessageBlock` props. Affected files include `cli/src/chat.tsx`, `cli/src/components/message-block.tsx`, `cli/src/hooks/use-message-renderer.tsx`, and `cli/src/hooks/use-scroll-management.ts`.

eli5.text: When you expand or collapse an agent or tool branch in the CLI chat, the view no longer automatically scrolls that section to a fixed position near the top. The program that tracked each branch's on-screen location and moved the scroll window to it has been deleted. As a result, expanding a branch keeps the current scroll position, so long conversations no longer jump around as you open nested replies.

ai.title: CLI inertial scroll removed for quadratic
ai.summary: Replaced `InertialScrollAccel` with `createChatScrollAcceleration` in `cli/src/chat.tsx` and `cli/src/utils/chat-scroll-accel.ts`. Deleted ~170 lines of inertial physics code (momentum, impulse windows, decay). Kept quadratic acceleration with adjusted multipliers. Affects CLI scroll behavior only.

eli5.text: When you scroll through a long conversation in the command-line chat, the program used to make scrolling feel smooth by predicting how fast you want to move based on how quickly you spin your scroll wheel. That predictive physics engine has been removed; scrolling now moves at a steady, direct rate tied only to how hard you scroll, without building or losing momentum. The effect is visible to anyone running the CLI chat today, and you’d notice scrolling no longer accelerates or drifts to a stop.

ai.title: Add ghostty scroll multiplier and refactor env detection
ai.summary: Refactored `resolveScrollEnvironment` in `cli/src/utils/chat-scroll-accel.ts` to use a centralized `ENVIRONMENTS` array and `ENV_MULTIPLIERS` map, adding explicit support for `ghostty` (0.3) and `vscode` (0.3). Default scroll multiplier changed from undefined/1 to 0.2 when no environment is detected, and `slow` override now applies a 0.5x factor to the detected environment's multiplier instead of a fixed 0.12. Replaced `clamp` with `Math.min`/`Math.round` for scroll row calculation.

eli5.text: The assistant now detects when you're using the Ghostty or VS Code terminal and adjusts how fast the text scrolls to match each one's expected speed. If you're using one of those programs, the scroll speed will feel smoother and correctly tuned. If the assistant can't tell which terminal you're using, it falls back to a moderate default speed instead of scrolling at full speed.

ai.title: chat-scroll-accel clamp back
ai.summary: Replaced inline Math.min with clamp utility in QuadraticScrollAccel. Enforces minimum 1 row bound for scroll acceleration calculation. Scope limited to cli/src/utils/chat-scroll-accel.ts.

eli5.text: When you scroll through the chat in the CLI, the scroll speed is calculated based on how many recent scroll ticks have happened. Previously, the software used a quick inline calculation that could sometimes cause issues if the multiplier produced a very small or zero value. The developers replaced that with a safer, reusable helper that ensures the scroll acceleration always stays within a minimum of 1 row and a maximum set by the software. If you looked at the code, you'd see the calculation now uses a clamp function instead of directly calling Math.min, making the scrolling behavior more predictable and preventing edge-case bugs.

ai.title: Linear scroll acceleration on macOS
ai.summary: Switches chat scrolling to linear acceleration on macOS via `LinearScrollAccel` in `cli/src/utils/chat-scroll-accel.ts`. Renames `CODEBUFF_SCROLL_MODE` to `CODEBUFF_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER`, adds `fast` override, and applies platform-specific class selection. Default multiplier now uses `ENV_MULTIPLIERS.default` constant.

eli5.text: When you scroll through the chat window in the assistant on a Mac, the scrolling now moves at a steady, constant speed instead of speeding up the longer you hold or roll. The app decided this just for Macs by picking the new steady-speed scrolling method automatically when it detects you are on macOS, while keeping the previous behavior for other operating systems. The speed can still be adjusted up or down through a setting that now understands the words slow, fast, and default, and the base speed the app falls back to is set by a single shared number. If you watched the code, you would see a new scrolling class that always scrolls the same amount each moment, and the app choosing between that and the old speeding-up version based on your computer.

ai.title: QuadraticScrollAccel buffer for macOS
ai.summary: QuadraticScrollAccel now uses fractional accumulator buffer instead of rounding per tick. createChatScrollAcceleration drops platform check, always returns QuadraticScrollAccel. Affects cli/src/utils/chat-scroll-accel.ts. Reset clears buffer alongside tickHistory.

eli5.text: When you rapidly scroll through conversations in the CLI, the assistant now accumulates smaller scroll amounts in a buffer instead of rounding each tick, resulting in smoother scroll behavior. This applies specifically to macOS users, as the platform check that previously routed macOS to a different scroll handler has been removed. The scroll state now resets both the buffer and history simultaneously when interrupted, ensuring clean state management. The change is live as of the current CLI implementation.

ai.title: Remove Cursor support from CLI scroll acceleration
ai.summary: Drops 'cursor' from ENVIRONMENTS and INERTIAL_HINT_VARS in cli/src/utils/chat-scroll-accel.ts, removing CURSOR, CURSOR_TERM, and CURSOR_TERMINAL detection. Adjusts ENV_MULTIPLIERS: ghostty 0.3 to 0.2, vscode 0.3 to 0.05, default 0.3 to 0.05. Scope limited to CLI scroll acceleration logic.

eli5.text: If you ran the command-line tool inside the Cursor editor, the smooth-scrolling speed-up that kicks in automatically no longer recognizes that editor and falls back to a gentler default. The tool no longer detects Cursor specifically, and the speed multipliers for Ghostty and VS Code were also lowered, so on those setups the scroll acceleration is a bit slower. Nothing breaks, you just won’t get the Cursor-tuned boost anymore, and the default and VS Code responses feel noticeably tamer.

ai.title: Simplify CLI title screen and agent list rendering
ai.summary: Removed dynamic greeting and default agent header from `cli/src/chat.tsx`, replacing verbose status text with concise command/directory info. `cli/src/components/message-block.tsx` drops agent list truncation logic, rendering full lists via `ToolCallItem` instead of `AgentBranchItem` previews. Scope limited to CLI chat interface components.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant in your terminal, instead of greeting you by name and showing a verbose status line, it now displays only your current folder and a few simple commands. In chat, long lists of assistant choices that used to be trimmed and hidden are now shown in full, so you see every option without any truncation. The change affects anyone who launches the terminal assistant and scrolls through its messages, and it is live today.

ai.title: Fix web build and CI for agents server aggregator
ai.summary: Web build and CI pipeline updated to fix agents server aggregator issues. New prebuild script `web/scripts/prebuild-agents-cache.ts` validates data pipeline post-build. CI workflow `web` package tests run via `bun run test --runInBand`, and interactive debug shell removed. Health check endpoint `web/src/app/api/healthz/route.ts` now warms agents cache. Jest config ignores e2e tests; Playwright config port aligned with dev server.

eli5.text: The website that shows agents and their metrics now checks its data connection during the build process, so if the connection to the database is broken, the build fails immediately instead of silently producing an empty site. After the build, the site also warms up its cache automatically when the hosting platform (Render) pings its health check endpoint, meaning the agents data is ready to serve the moment real traffic arrives. The automated tests that previously ran one file at a time now run together in sequence, and the old interactive debugging tool that used to open on test failures has been removed, so if something breaks, engineers will need to reproduce the issue locally rather than debugging it live.

ai.title: Refactor CLI scroll acceleration to support CODEBUFFSCROLLMULTIPLIER
ai.summary: The `createChatScrollAcceleration` function in `cli/src/utils/chat-scroll-accel.ts` was refactored to replace boolean `enabled` states and string-based `slow`/`fast` overrides with a numeric `multiplier` derived from the `CODEBUFF_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER` environment variable. The `resolveScrollEnvironment` function now parses this variable as a float (defaulting to 1.0 if invalid) and combines it with environment-specific base multipliers for Zed, Ghostty, and VS Code. This change removes the previous `INERTIAL_HINT_VARS` logic in favor of `ENVIRONMENT_TYPE_VARS` and simplifies the `ScrollEnvironment` type to use a `type` field instead of `hint` and `override` properties.

eli5.text: The terminal-based assistant now lets you control how fast the chat window scrolls by setting a number in a special environment variable called CODEBUFF_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER. Instead of picking between fixed slow or fast presets, you can now type any decimal value to fine-tune the speed, which gets combined with the specific adjustments already made for popular terminal programs like Zed, Ghostty, and VS Code. This replaces the old on/off toggle system that previously had less flexible control over the scrolling behavior.

ai.title: CLI agent mode toggle gains hover interaction and column layout
ai.summary: AgentModeToggle now expands on mouse hover with 1s close delay, replacing click-only toggle. Collapsed state arrow repositioned to left of label. Expanded layout shifts from horizontal segments with shared borders to vertical columns with per-segment borders. Affects cli/src/components/agent-mode-toggle.tsx only.

eli5.text: When you move your cursor over the mode switch in the command-line assistant, it now unfolds automatically instead of requiring a click. If you look at it, the arrow for the current mode shifts to the left of its label, and the expanded options spread out in vertical columns rather than a single horizontal strip. The panel also lingers for one second after you move the cursor away before collapsing again.

ai.title: CLI agent mode toggle adds selection menu
ai.summary: AgentModeToggle component in cli/src/components/agent-mode-toggle.tsx introduces an expanded state for selecting FAST, MAX, or PLAN modes directly. Previously a simple toggle, it now renders a bordered menu when active, allowing users to click specific modes. The chat.tsx file passes the new onSelectMode prop to handle direct mode switching. Emoji labels were removed in favor of text-only identifiers.

eli5.text: If you use the assistant from the command line, you can now click the mode toggle to see a small menu that lets you switch directly between FAST, MAX, and PLAN instead of just turning the current mode on or off. The menu shows up next to the existing toggle, displays plain text labels, and disappears after you pick a mode. This change only affects the command-line tool and is available today in version 25.11.0.

ai.title: CLI: agent status line and hover delay
ai.summary: Added right-aligned agent status line to chat UI. Implemented 250ms hover delay for mode toggle to prevent accidental triggers. Scope: cli/src/chat.tsx, cli/src/components/agent-mode-toggle.tsx. Detail: Agent display name resolves from loadedAgentsData using current mode or explicit agentId.

eli5.text: When you open the chat in the command-line tool, you will now see a short status line on the right side that shows which assistant is currently active. You will also notice that the mode toggle button no longer reacts when you briefly hover the cursor over it; it waits a moment before responding, so accidental switches are less likely. Together these tweaks make the chat header clearer and the mode button steadier to use.

ai.title: Cancel pending timeout on agent mode toggle press
ai.summary: handlePress now clears openTimeoutRef before executing toggle logic. Prevents delayed UI state conflicts when clicking current mode. Scope limited to cli/src/components/agent-mode-toggle.tsx.

eli5.text: When you click the mode toggle button to collapse or expand it, any delayed opening animation that was scheduled stops immediately, so the toggle responds to your click right away instead of after a short lag. This only affects people using the command-line version of the assistant and clicking the toggle for the currently selected mode. You'd notice the toggle opens or closes instantly when clicked, with no brief delay where it appeared stuck.

ai.title: CLI scroll: Increase rolling window
ai.summary: Default `rollingWindowMs` in `QuadraticScrollAccel` increased from 50 to 100 in `cli/src/utils/chat-scroll-accel.ts`. `ghostty` scroll multiplier reduced from 0.2 to 0.15. Adjusts scroll acceleration behavior for smoother terminal interaction.

eli5.text: When you scroll through conversation history in the terminal chat, messages now move more smoothly and gradually instead of accelerating suddenly. The scroll behavior was tuned so the terminal keeps track of your scrolling gestures for a bit longer and applies gentler scaling, making it feel less jerky. If you use the CLI chat in a Ghostty terminal, you'll notice scrolling reacts more calmly to your input. This change is live today.

ai.title: Update chat scroll acceleration multipliers for Zed and Ghostty
ai.summary: Chat scroll acceleration multipliers for Zed and Ghostty environments updated in `cli/src/utils/chat-scroll-accel.ts`. Zed multiplier changed from 0.015 to 0.07, Ghostty from 0.15 to 0.2. This adjustment modifies the scroll speed behavior within the CLI chat interface for these specific terminal environments.

eli5.text: When you're using the app inside Zed or Ghostty terminal programs, the chat window now scrolls faster as you type or receive messages. Previously the scroll speed was slower in these two environments compared to other terminals; the multipliers that control how quickly the view catches up to new content were raised, so you'll notice the viewport keeping pace more briskly when the text moves fast. This affects only people running the chat inside Zed or Ghostty; users in other terminals see no difference.

ai.title: Chat scroll uses constant acceleration
ai.summary: CLI chat scroll switched to ConstantScrollAccel. Replaces QuadraticScrollAccel in createChatScrollAcceleration. ENV_MULTIPLIERS unified to 0.5 for zed, ghostty, vscode, default. Handles negative scroll buffers via Math.ceil.

eli5.text: When you scroll up or down in the chat window inside the CLI, the scrolling speed now stays constant instead of accelerating the longer you hold or repeat the scroll command. This affects anyone using the CLI in any environment (Zed, Ghostty, VSCode, or default), since the speed multipliers for all environments were unified to the same value. If you watched the scrolling behavior, you would notice it no longer builds up momentum over time, and any negative scroll buffer values are handled properly using ceiling rounding instead of flooring.

ai.title: CLI scroll multiplier set to 1
ai.summary: Scroll acceleration multiplier in `cli/src/utils/chat-scroll-accel.ts` changed from 0.5 to 1 for all environments (zed, ghostty, vscode, default). This adjusts the scroll sensitivity within the CLI chat interface. Scope is limited to the CLI utility file. The `ENV_MULTIPLIERS` constant now enforces a 1:1 scroll ratio.

eli5.text: When you use the CLI chat and scroll through the conversation, your scroll gestures are now less sensitive and feel more natural. Previously, the interface applied half-speed scrolling that made navigation feel sluggish; now your scroll input moves one-to-one with your actions. This affects anyone typing in the command-line chat, making it easier to review past messages without over-scrolling.

ai.title: Fix codesearch flag injection with --
ai.summary: Added `--` separator to `rg` arguments in `handleCodeSearch` within `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts`. Prevents patterns starting with `-` from being misparsed as flags by ripgrep. Ensures correct search execution for such patterns.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to search the codebase for a term that starts with a hyphen (like -config), it now finds the right matches instead of thinking that term is a command-line option. The search tool adds a special -- separator before your search text so the underlying search engine treats everything after it as a literal query. This only affects internal code-search behavior, so nothing visible changes in the app today.

ai.title: CLI bang prefix executes terminal commands
ai.summary: CLI router detects leading `!` to trigger `runTerminalCommand` from SDK, bypassing model. Sync execution renders stdout in tool block. `env` type in SDK relaxed to allow undefined values. Files: `cli/src/commands/router.ts`, `sdk/src/index.ts`.

eli5.text: You can now run a terminal command directly from the assistant's command line by typing an exclamation mark followed by the command (for example, "!git status"), and the output will appear in the same area where the assistant normally shows its answers instead of going through the assistant at all. This only works when you start a message with that exclamation mark in the CLI, and it bypasses the assistant so the command runs immediately and synchronously right in the terminal.

ai.title: Add readfiles tool component
ai.summary: New `ReadFilesComponent` added to CLI tool registry. Renders `read_files` tool calls with first file on name line, next two on newlines, rest inline. No expand/collapse support.

eli5.text: When the assistant wants to show you the contents of several files it just read, it now draws them in the chat with a nicer layout: the tool name sits on the first line next to the first file path, the next two file paths each get their own line, and any remaining paths are listed together in a compact row. This only affects how that particular tool result looks in the terminal-based CLI, so if you run the assistant in that interface you’ll notice the cleaner grouping whenever it reads multiple files at once. It went live today with no switches to flip.

ai.summary: Shortens labels for `code_search` and `list_directory` components to 'Search' and 'List' respectively. `code_search` summary format changes to include `cwd` and removes noisy regex `flags`, while `tool-call-item` updates text wrapping to 'word' mode for better layout. eli5.text: When the assistant tells you about the code files it's looking at or the folders it's listing, those messages now show shorter, cleaner labels ('Search' and 'List') and pack in the useful details like the current folder, without the clutter of technical pattern flags. Text in the tool result rows also wraps at word boundaries instead of running on, so long lines stay readable in the terminal. These tweaks only affect how the command-line tool formats its output, so if you're running it today, you'll notice neater, more compact summaries for code-search and directory-listing actions.

ai.title: Fix glob tool path matching when cwd set
ai.summary: The `glob` tool now correctly filters files when a `cwd` is specified. Paths are made relative to `cwd` before micromatch, then converted back to project-relative paths. Fixes incorrect matching logic in `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant's file-searching tool now returns the correct files when you ask it to look in a specific folder. You would notice by getting only the matching files from that folder instead of getting files from the wrong location. The tool now properly filters files based on the folder you asked it to search in before using the search pattern.

ai.title: Tweak agent toggle timing and layout
ai.summary: Agent mode toggle in `cli/src/components/agent-mode-toggle.tsx` now opens instantly and closes after 100ms. Layout logic updated to always append current mode to `ALL_MODES` list rather than filtering and reordering, simplifying active state detection and frame rendering.

eli5.text: When you hover over the agent mode menu, it now appears instantly instead of after a noticeable delay, and it disappears quickly once you move your mouse away. The layout of the menu items has been streamlined so the currently selected mode is always shown in a consistent position with a cleaner visual style. These adjustments make the toggle feel snappier and easier to read while you're switching between modes.
